title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)
talk_summary: A fireside chat with Turbopuffer CEO Simon Eskildsen covering his path from Shopify infra to building an S3-backed vector database, emphasizing napkin-math capacity reasoning, simplicity-first engineering, and honest capital allocation. Most of the content is career narrative and company philosophy; the transferable mechanisms are fault-injection testing via a proxy, back-of-envelope performance modeling, and simplicity as a design constraint.

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a thin layer-7 proxy (Toxiproxy) between app and database that can simulate slow/down/corrupt DB conditions via API calls, so failure-handling tests run in CI against real drivers instead of mocks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not mocking the low-level drivers but you're testing the drivers and their failure handling as well so then this entire matrix could be implemented in CI
takeaways.numbers: uncovered tens of issues in the MySQL driver and Rails

takeaways.technique: Napkin-math capacity modeling before adopting a tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains a table of hardware cost/throughput numbers (DRAM bandwidth, S3 roundtrip, fsync latency, $/GB) and uses it to sanity-check benchmarks and reject implausible infrastructure decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this should take 10 millisecond you tell me the benchmark takes 10 one of us is wrong
takeaways.numbers: S3 P99 ~200ms for 256-512KB object; fsync ~1ms; MySQL ~10k writes/s via batching

takeaways.technique: Simplicity-first MVP, ship the dumbest version
takeaways.what_they_do: Shipped a single-server, reverse-proxy-cached S3 prototype rather than a full LSM implementation, then iterated once real users appeared.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It was the simplest possible version of what it could be

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately support many CPU/instance SKUs so they can take whatever capacity is available rather than being locked to one machine type.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are very very good at using a lot of very different SKs

takeaways.what_they_do: Enumerates explicit reasons to raise capital (R&D, growth, ego, employee liquidity, strategic, M&A) and only acts when the reason is honest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to be very honest about what reason you are raising in those six
